description: Wave 0 adversarial English pass over 134 new and changed keys (15 already-ruled keys excluded). Remaining keys were read with their render sites and each had one plausible reading.

entries.complaint: "Base" collides with the Base scenario and does not say base of what
readings: base of the structure including its foundation
entries.resolution: Reverted by the orchestrator: "Base elevation" is the name Tom built and tested on feat/tank-ground (2026-10-11). The collision with the Base scenario is real and is put to him as a question, not decided here.

entries.complaint: "Depth" alone reads as pipe burial depth or depth of cover
readings: depth of water in the tank
burial depth of a node or pipe
entries.resolution: Reverted by the orchestrator: a results column heading, where width is king (CLAUDE.md). The column sits under a tank context, so Depth reads as water depth there.

entries.complaint: dangling "zoom to" leaves the object of the preposition open
readings: drag a rectangle that you zoom to
zoom to the area the rectangle encloses
entries.resolution: Rewritten: "Zoom Window: drag a rectangle to zoom to." -> "Zoom Window: drag a rectangle on the map to zoom to that area."

entries.complaint: "named" for a pattern: the visitor-facing term for a library reference is the ID, as in lpn_link_end_unknown
readings: no pattern carries this descriptive name
entries.resolution: Rewritten: "No pattern in this project is named {id}, so the junction was left as it was." -> "No pattern in this project has the ID {id}, so the junction was left as it was."

entries.complaint: "unselects whatever is selected" departs from the Select/Selection vocabulary
entries.resolution: Rewritten: "Use this mode to change, move, and drag assets and text on the map, or to pan the map. This is the default mode for the map. Pressing Esc a second time unselects whatever is selected." -> "Use this mode to change, move, and drag assets and text on the map, or to pan the map. This is the default mode for the map. Pressing Esc a second time clears the selection."

entries.complaint: "also exists outside" has two possible subjects, the node or the link
readings: the node exists outside the scenario
the link exists outside the scenario
entries.resolution: Rewritten: "{id} is not deleted, because link {link} ends on it and also exists outside {scenario}. To delete both, delete them in the {base} scenario." -> "{id} is not deleted, because link {link} ends on it, and that link also exists outside {scenario}. To delete both, delete them in the {base} scenario."

entries.complaint: "sharper-than-screen" is an unusual compound; "to mark up and then copy" does not say what is marked up
readings: the map area is marked up before the picture
sharper means focus rather than resolution
entries.resolution: Rewritten: "Take a sharper-than-screen picture of the map area you drag, to mark up and then copy into a report with the Copy button. Click without dragging to take the whole map." -> "Take a picture of the map area you drag, at a higher resolution than the screen. Mark it up, then copy it into a report with the Copy button. Click without dragging to take the whole map."

entries.complaint: "the current selection" collides with the reserved map-selection sense; the shortcut carries selected text from the page
entries.resolution:
Rewritten: "
?Open the guide at the control under the pointer or holding focus.
F1Open the guide at the entry for the box that has f" -> "
?Open the guide at the control under the pointer or holding focus.
F1Open the guide at the entry for the box that has f"

entries.complaint: "across / down" does not say which key goes which way; "Navigate" for backward movement is vague
readings: Tab goes across and Enter goes down
entries.resolution:
Rewritten: "
Arrow keysNavigate.
Tab, EnterFinish entry and navigate across / down one cell.
Shift+Tab, Shift+Enter" -> "
Arrow keysNavigate.
Tab, EnterFinish the entry and move one cell across (Tab) or down (Enter).
Shift+T"

entries.complaint: Copy button is not named
entries.resolution: Copy is the visible button label beside the heading; one reading.

entries.complaint: "in chosen units" could be unit set or unit menu
entries.resolution: Established phrasing for the unit the visitor chose in the menu; Tom's choose/chosen rule for menu options.

entries.complaint: roughness symbol set per method
entries.resolution: Each symbol is named with its method and the typical values are stated; one reading.

entries.complaint: "From {menu}" could be origin of a movement
entries.resolution: Heading over a group of boxes opened from that menu (js guide builder); {menu} is a menu name, one reading.

entries.complaint: "Guide" noun or verb
entries.resolution: Menu item beside Help; "Guide" as noun is the only reading in a toolbar menu and the title of the box.

entries.complaint: "Contents" as table of contents or things contained
entries.resolution: Sits on a rail with the guide entries listed under it and next to Hide/Show contents; one reading.

entries.complaint: "Current"/"All" lack a noun
entries.resolution: The radio group heading (Tables or Scenarios) supplies the noun at render; gender agreement is the translator's routine task. A split into two keys per group is not worth 4 retranslations.

entries.complaint: "All" lacks a noun
entries.resolution: See lpn_export_table_current.

entries.complaint: Yes/No without the question
entries.resolution: Answers lpn_split_pipe_ask, shown directly above the buttons; a Yes/No button is standard in every language.

entries.complaint: "method" is unexplained
entries.resolution: The panel immediately offers Node, Free point and Coordinates; one reading.

entries.complaint: "text size" may mean the Text asset
entries.resolution: Matches the setting "Text size (pixels)" which scales every label; the setting name is the referent.

entries.complaint: "chosen" vs stated/selected for curve references
entries.resolution: A drop-down option, so choose/chosen is correct per the menu/dialog rule.

entries.complaint: "ends in three periods" is an unusual way to say ellipsis
entries.resolution: The three characters are shown literally in the file; the string is exact and unambiguous.

entries.complaint: Query keywords (Everything, equal to, n highest) must stay English per the text, but the table mixes them with translated prose, so it is unclear whether the example column should be translated.
readings: kept all query words and examples in English, prose translated
entries.resolution: The guide states that the English query words are accepted in every language: code samples keep the English words, and prose names the control as the translated page shows it.

entries.complaint: 'Zoom Window:' reads as a menu name; unclear if it must match the translated toolbar label.
entries.resolution: 'Zoom Window' names the tool; render it as the translated toolbar label names it.

entries.complaint: 'mixing and water age' and the long reason are dense; hard to render as a single clear sentence in a low-resource language.
entries.resolution: Dense but single-reading; a descriptive rendering in two sentences is acceptable in the low-resource tier.

entries.complaint: "Workspace" is ambiguous between a project folder and the saved window layout; the tip shows it is the layout.
readings: Работна среда (saved layout of boxes and panes)
entries.resolution: The tip disambiguates (the saved window layout), and the translator read it correctly.

entries.complaint: The table lists query words (equal to, above, n highest) that the guide says are accepted in every language, but the Czech UI shows translated words (rovno, větší než); unclear which the guide should show.
readings: kept the English words the query accepts, as typed
translated them to match the Czech Condition list
entries.resolution: The guide states that the English query words are accepted in every language: code samples keep the English words, and prose names the control as the translated page shows it.

entries.complaint: 'Layers' and 'attributes' are CAD terms; unclear if Layer names the DXF layer or the app's alternative.
readings: DXF layers (hladiny), with the English term in parentheses
entries.resolution: In a DXF note, 'layers' and 'attributes' are the CAD meanings, and 'scale the blocks' is an instruction to the reader.

entries.complaint: identical to English is correct
entries.resolution: Cognate: identical to English is correct for es; exempted per language in translation_exempt_keys.json.

entries.complaint: identical to English is correct
readings: Guide (the French word is the same)
entries.resolution: Cognate: identical to English is correct for fr; exempted per language in translation_exempt_keys.json.

entries.complaint: Quotes the box text "Change 4 assets?" but the hi value of lpn_replace_preview is still English, so the guide and the page disagree if that key is later translated.
readings: left the quoted English as shown on the page today
entries.resolution: The quoted labels are keys of their own (lpn_replace_preview, the Change them and Change what was found keys) and are translated; the guide quotes those translated values. The hi report that lpn_replace_preview was English was wrong: the hi file holds a translation.

entries.complaint: "Color nodes by:" is a label; the sentence runs it inline as a name, which reads oddly with a colon.
readings: used the hi label of lpn_color_node_field without colon
entries.resolution: A quoted label may keep its colon or drop it inline, per the language's punctuation.

entries.complaint: identical to English is correct
readings: Min (standard Indonesian abbreviation of minimum, paired with Maks)
entries.resolution: Cognate: identical to English is correct for id; exempted per language in translation_exempt_keys.json.

entries.complaint: identical to English is correct
readings: (default: {id}) — 'default' is the established Indonesian software term and the file already uses it (Pola kebutuhan default)
entries.resolution: Cognate: identical to English is correct for id; exempted per language in translation_exempt_keys.json.

entries.complaint: identical to English is correct
entries.resolution: Cognate: identical to English is correct for id; exempted per language in translation_exempt_keys.json.

entries.complaint: identical to English is correct
readings: Min is the standard Italian abbreviation
a longer word would not fit the column
entries.resolution: Cognate: identical to English is correct for it; exempted per language in translation_exempt_keys.json.

entries.complaint: identical to English is correct
readings: Max is the standard Italian abbreviation
a longer word would not fit the column
entries.resolution: Cognate: identical to English is correct for it; exempted per language in translation_exempt_keys.json.

entries.complaint: identical to English is correct
readings: No is the Italian word for no
entries.resolution: Cognate: identical to English is correct for it; exempted per language in translation_exempt_keys.json.

entries.complaint: 'one file for each parameter' is ambiguous between per-parameter files and one file per measured quantity.
readings: one file for each measured parameter (pressure, flow)
entries.resolution: One file per measured quantity (pressure, flow, level): the two readings are the same.

entries.complaint: 'vertex' has no established Pashto engineering term; used the Arabic-derived 'رأس' (corner point).
entries.resolution: Descriptive rendering is right for the low-resource tier.

entries.complaint: identical to English is correct
entries.resolution: Cognate: identical to English is correct for ro; exempted per language in translation_exempt_keys.json.

entries.complaint: 'Zoom Window with no fit first' has no clear object, so it is unclear whether the W key skips fitting or opens the window tool.
readings: W starts the Zoom Window tool directly without fitting the network first
W fits the network then starts Zoom Window
entries.resolution: Two languages (sw, ur) independently could not parse 'For Zoom Window with no fit first'. Rewritten after the sprint to: 'Fit the whole network to the map window. To zoom to a rectangle you drag instead, press W or click the small triangle in the corner of the Zoom to fit toolbar button. See also the zoom controls at the upper right of the map.' Held back from the baseline (--except), so the next sprint retranslates it.

entries.complaint: The quoted button labels 'Change them' and 'Change what was found' have no confirmed Swahili UI counterparts, so quoted names may not match the shipped buttons.
entries.resolution: The quoted labels are keys of their own (lpn_replace_preview, the Change them and Change what was found keys) and are translated; the guide quotes those translated values. The hi report that lpn_replace_preview was English was wrong: the hi file holds a translation.

entries.complaint: 'attributes 1 unit high' and 'scale the blocks to set the text height' are ambiguous about whether the instruction is to the reader or a statement of fact.
readings: advice to the CAD user: scale blocks to change text height
entries.resolution: In a DXF note, 'layers' and 'attributes' are the CAD meanings, and 'scale the blocks' is an instruction to the reader.

entries.complaint: 'For Zoom Window with no fit first' is elliptical and can be read two ways.
readings: To use Zoom Window without fitting first, press W or click the corner triangle
Zoom Window as a separate alternative to fitting
entries.resolution: Two languages (sw, ur) independently could not parse 'For Zoom Window with no fit first'. Rewritten after the sprint to: 'Fit the whole network to the map window. To zoom to a rectangle you drag instead, press W or click the small triangle in the corner of the Zoom to fit toolbar button. See also the zoom controls at the upper right of the map.' Held back from the baseline (--except), so the next sprint retranslates it.

entries.complaint: Condition names are shown in English in the code samples but are translated in the UI; unclear whether the prose should name the English or the UI words.
readings: prose uses the Urdu UI condition names, code samples stay English
entries.resolution: The guide states that the English query words are accepted in every language: code samples keep the English words, and prose names the control as the translated page shows it.
